objective: Proof: a knot freezes every native tree without pins, so that boundary values can force the root edge either way at every depth, exactly when every place takes both values on its excluded tuples; census of the 14 such knots, including the six open knots, not-all-equal and parity; consequence for decay uniform over boundary pins, and the explanation of ticket C's refutation.
status: Proved by NATIVE-APPROX-20261024-001D-P001: a knot freezes every native tree without pins (boundary values can force the root edge either way at every depth) exactly when its excluded tuples take both values at every place; at a one-way place the root marginal stays on one side of 1/2. Exactly 14 knots are two-way forcing, including the six open knots, not-all-equal and parity, so decay uniform over boundary pins fails for the open knots without signalling hardness; this explains ticket C's refutation.
title: Two-way forcing freezes native trees
